tasks.short: Read committee papers, attend and decide, write policy texts, take minutes when on duty and track action points.

steps.what: Teacher reads the committee papers before the meeting
Teacher serves on academic and administrative committees in meetings
Teacher writes policy texts and advice for the committee
Teacher takes the minutes when it is their turn

loop.input: The meeting transcript, recorded with all members' consent, and the agenda.
loop.output: Draft minutes per agenda item: decisions, action points with owner and date.
loop.check: Code checks every agenda item has an entry and every action point has an owner and date; the minute taker edits the draft and the chair approves it at the next meeting.
loop.stop: One draft per meeting; without consent or on failure the teacher writes the minutes.
loop.why_not_simpler: Discussion is free talk; a template cannot turn it into decisions and actions.

steps.what: Teacher chases action points by e-mail

tasks.design: With all members' consent, the meeting tool transcribes the meeting and a bounded step drafts minutes per agenda item, which the minute taker edits. Action points go into a shared list in the committee's document space ({DOCS}) that reminds owners before their date. Reading papers, deciding and writing policy stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Minutes were written from notes and action points chased by e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Meeting tools transcribe, and language models can draft minutes from a transcript.
tasks.still_hard: Some members will not agree to recording; then minutes are written by hand.
tasks.human_edge: Finding a policy that both teachers and students can live with.

reach.learn: Whether drafted minutes cut secretary time.

evidence.claim: Meeting tools transcribe meetings, and language models can draft minutes for editing.
Systems able to monitor staff, such as recorded meetings, need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from committee papers to action points; implementing policy is outside.
Input contract: papers and agenda from the committee secretary; fallback is minutes by hand.
Reading, deciding and policy writing do not change.
Recordings are deleted once minutes are approved.
research_questions: Are action points finished on time more often?

incremental.description: Chair asks for recording consent at each meeting.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is reading and meetings.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Look up the student's progress, advise in a meeting, answer e-mailed curriculum questions from the regulations, note the advice and refer on.

steps.what: Teacher gathers the student's results and progress from several screens
Teacher advises students on academic and vocational curricula and career issues
Teacher answers e-mailed questions about electives, minors and placements

loop.input: The student's e-mailed question, the programme's course catalogue and its education and examination regulations.
loop.output: A draft reply quoting the matching catalogue entry or regulation article with its link.
loop.check: Code checks every quote matches the source word for word and comes from the current academic year; personal circumstances or exceptions go to the teacher unanswered; the teacher reads, edits and sends every reply.
loop.stop: One draft per question; no matching passage means the teacher writes the reply.
loop.why_not_simpler: Students ask in their own words; catalogue search misses rules spread over several articles.

steps.what: Teacher writes a note of the advice in the student file
Teacher refers students to the study adviser or career service

tasks.design: A progress view in the student information system ({OTHER}) shows results, credits and planned courses on one screen before the talk. For e-mailed curriculum questions, a bounded step drafts replies that quote the course catalogue and the education and examination regulations, and the teacher edits and sends them; personal cases go to the teacher directly. Advice notes use a short template. The advising talk and referrals stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Progress was gathered from several screens and every e-mail answered from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Student systems show progress in one view, and catalogues and regulations are published per year.
tasks.still_hard: Career advice depends on the student's situation and wishes; no source covers it.
tasks.human_edge: Helping a doubting student see which path fits them.
tasks.altitude: The teacher edits quoted replies instead of looking up every rule.

reach.learn: Whether quoted replies cut repeat questions.

evidence.claim: Education and examination regulations and course catalogues are published per programme and year.
AI used for admission or evaluating learning outcomes is high-risk; drafting replies on regulations is not covered.

assumptions: Boundary: from the student's record and questions to advice and referrals; exam board decisions are outside.
Input contract: results and credits from the student information system; catalogue and regulations published by the programme office; fallback is lookup by hand.
The talk and referrals do not change.
research_questions: How many questions match a catalogue or regulation passage?

incremental.description: Programme office loads the new year's catalogue and regulations.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is the advising talk.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Set office-hour times, agree slots with students, meet students, send follow-up material and note agreements.

steps.what: Teacher chooses the weekly office hours
Teacher agrees meeting times with students by e-mail
Teacher meets students in office hours to advise and assist them
Teacher e-mails follow-up material to students
Teacher notes agreements in the student file

tasks.design: Students book office-hour slots on a booking page linked to the teacher's calendar ({CALENDAR}), only within the times the teacher has set, and get a confirmation automatically. Meeting students, sending material and notes stay with the teacher; notes use a short template.
tasks.previous_blocker: Slots were agreed one by one by e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Booking pages linked to calendars are standard.
tasks.still_hard: Students in crisis do not book; they knock on the door.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing the student behind the question about a deadline.

evidence.claim: Booking pages linked to calendars let students book within set times and send confirmations.
Student names and booking reasons are personal data; keep reasons short.

assumptions: Boundary: from setting times to notes; formal mentoring is outside.
Input contract: teaching timetable from the scheduling office; fallback is e-mail.
Meetings and follow-up do not change.
Students' time is outside the teacher's savings.
research_questions: Do more students use office hours once they can book?

incremental.description: Teacher sets up the booking page once.

approvals.approved_version: The office-hour times set by the teacher in s1; bookings outside them are not offered.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most of this task is meeting students.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Search and screen the literature, design studies and collect data, analyse, write the manuscript, format references and submit.

steps.what: Teacher searches literature databases and reads abstracts to find relevant studies

loop.input: Abstracts returned by the teacher's saved database searches and the written inclusion criteria.
loop.output: Include or exclude per abstract with the criterion and quoted sentence it rests on.
loop.check: The teacher reviews every include and a random sample of excludes; code checks each record resolves by DOI or catalogue entry and drops any that does not.
loop.stop: One pass per search update; if the sample shows wrong excludes, the teacher screens the batch by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Inclusion criteria need reading of free text; keyword filters miss or over-include too many.

steps.what: Teacher designs studies and collects data in the field of knowledge
Teacher analyses the data
Teacher writes the manuscript to publish findings
Teacher formats references and the manuscript to the journal's style
Teacher submits to the journal and answers reviewers

tasks.design: Saved searches in the literature databases ({OTHER}) rerun on a schedule, and a bounded step screens new abstracts against the teacher's written criteria, quoting the sentence each decision rests on; the teacher reviews includes and a sample of excludes. A reference manager formats references to the journal's style and checks each resolves by DOI. Study design, data, analysis, writing and submission stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Abstracts were screened one by one and references formatted by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Literature databases support saved searches, and language models can classify abstracts against written criteria.
tasks.still_hard: A wrongly excluded study can change a review's conclusion; sampling must be honest.
tasks.human_edge: Asking the question no one in the field has asked yet.
tasks.altitude: The teacher reviews screened abstracts instead of reading all of them.

reach.learn: Whether screened abstracts match double human screening.

evidence.claim: Scopus AI gives topic summaries and foundational papers.
Grant referees may not use generative AI; uploading a proposal breaches confidentiality.

assumptions: Boundary: from the research question to submission; funding applications are outside.
Input contract: search strings and inclusion criteria written by the teacher; journal styles from the reference manager; fallback is screening by hand.
Design, data, analysis and writing do not change.
No unpublished manuscripts or data go into external AI tools.
research_questions: How often does the sample of excludes contain a relevant study?

already_counted.description: Teacher reviews includes and a sample of excludes.

incremental.description: Teacher writes inclusion criteria precise enough to screen against.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Most research time is design, data and writing.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The teacher keeps advising, deciding and research judgement; minutes, rule lookups, scheduling and screening shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A teacher who spends saved hours with students and on research.
